title: Severe bleeding
summary: Apply firm direct pressure; use a tourniquet for life-threatening limb bleeding when available and trained.
sources: 2024 American Heart Association and American Red Cross Guidelines for First Aid — Severe External Bleeding
2025 International Consensus on First Aid Science With Treatment Recommendations (ILCOR CoSTR) — Hemostatic Dressings
actions: Ensure scene safety, use gloves or a barrier if available, and call emergency services immediately.
Apply firm direct pressure with gauze or clean cloth. If blood soaks through, add material on top and keep pressing.

For life-threatening bleeding from an arm or leg, apply a commercial tourniquet if available and you are trained: place it 5 to 7 cm (2 to 3 in) above the wound, not over a joint, tighten until bleeding stops, and record the time.
If a tourniquet cannot be used, continue direct pressure. If trained, pack a deep wound with plain or hemostatic gauze and maintain pressure.
Do not remove an embedded object; press around it and stabilize it. Keep the person lying down, warm, and monitored.
prohibitions: Do not repeatedly lift the dressing to inspect the wound.
Do not loosen or remove a tourniquet once effective.
Do not place a tourniquet on the neck, trunk, or a joint.
Do not remove an embedded object.
